the colloidal crystals of pore-expanded MSN were successfully synthesized using a controlled growth method, which is the first report of the synthesis of such colloidal crystals.
we fabricated colloidal crystal composed of pore-expanded colloidal MSNs by a controlled growth process.
we have developed a novel colloidal growth method for preparing colloidal crystals composed MSNs, which have a controllable pore diameter and are monodispersed enough to form colloids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication of colloids composed of pore-expanded nanoparticles.
the preparation of colloidal crystals of mesoporous silicas with controlled pore sizes, which is expected to expand nanomaterials applications.
the fabrication of colloids with a controllable particle size and a controllable pore structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have successfully prepared colloidal MSNs with controllable pore sizes by using a particle growth method.
we have successfully prepared colloidal crystals composed MSNs with a controlled pore size and a narrow size distribution by a sophisticated particle growth strategy.
we fabricated colloidal crystal composed of pore-expanded colloidal MSNs with the controllable pore size using a sophisticated particle synthesis method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

colloidal crystals with pore-expanded MSNs can be prepared using a sophisticated particle-growth method, which can be applied to the preparation of other colloidal crystals composed with various mesoporous materials.
we developed a novel method to prepare colloidal MSNs with a tunable pore size by a particle growth method and fabricated a colloidal crystal of MSNs with the pore-expanded MSNs.
we have developed a novel synthetic method of MSNs with controllable pore size and particle size.
The main takeaway from our work is that
colloidal crystals of mesoporous nanoparticles can be prepared by using a particle growth method with a controlled pore size expansion.
the pore size of mesoporous materials can be controlled by a particle growth method, which is useful for the fabrication of functional colloidal crystals composed by mesoporous particles.
the particle growth method can control the mesopore sizes of MSNs while retaining the particle monodispersity, which is essential for the fabrication of MSNs-based colloidal crystals.
